properties.title: Learning the natural history of human disease with generative transformers

membership.reason: Delphi-2M is a continuous-time generative transformer modelling lifetime multi-morbidity disease progression and sampling up to 20-year future health trajectories.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L1 generative population/EHR disease-trajectory world model (WT_EHR, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: 2.2M-param modified GPT-2 (12 layers, 12 heads, 120 dim) with continuous-age sin/cos encoding + exponential waiting-time head

properties.flow: Longitudinal ICD-10 + lifestyle prompt -> Delphi-2M continuous-time autoregressive sampling -> multi-disease rates & 20-year synthetic trajectories

properties.purpose: Multi-disease incidence forecasting, 20-year health trajectory sampling, and synthetic cohort generation.
properties.environment: UK Biobank (0.4M train, 0.47M longitudinal test) + external Danish registry (1.93M)

assertions.rationale: Continuous age at first diagnosis encoded via sine/cosine basis functions.
Continuous-time exponential waiting-time head + random 'no event' padding tokens (~1 per 5 years) + causal continuous-time mask.
Token embeddings over 1,258 ICD-10, sex, BMI, smoking, alcohol, and padding tokens.
Causal transformer hidden state over lifetime health trajectory.
Predicts disease rates conditional on full prior individual disease and lifestyle history.
Iteratively samples next disease event and continuous waiting time up to 20 years.
Modified GPT-2 autoregressive point-process/exponential waiting-time transformer.
Stochastic sampling of next diagnosis token and inter-event time.

Evaluated next-diagnosis-token prediction across >1,000 ICD-10 diagnoses (average age-stratified AUC ~0.76, 97% of diagnoses AUC > 0.5, death AUC 0.97, 10-year horizon AUC 0.70; external Danish registry validation on 1.93M individuals) and 20-year iterative trajectory rollout (17% year-1 token accuracy vs 12-13% age/sex baseline, Fig. 3c; note HbA1c outperformed Delphi on diabetes).
Population-scale multi-disease risk forecasting and synthetic trajectory generation.
Multi-disease AUC (~0.76 next-event, 0.70 at 10-year horizon) and 20-year synthetic trajectory incidence calibration.
5-year age-bracket rate calibration and inter-event time calibration (Fig. 1g).
Zero-shot external validation on 1.93M Danish disease registry individuals with no parameter changes.

evidence_fragments.content: We train this model, Delphi-2M, on data from 0.4 million UK Biobank participants and validate it using external data from 1.9 million Danish individuals with no change in parameters. Delphi-2M predicts the rates of more than 1,000 diseases, conditional on each individual’s past disease history, with accuracy comparable to that of existing single-disease models. Delphi-2M’s generative nature also enables sampling of synthetic future health trajectories, providing meaningful estimates of potential disease burden for up to 20 years

[paraphrase (visual p.3)] Figure 1 shows Delphi's modified GPT-2 architecture and study design: (a) lifetime trajectory tokens (sex, disease, lifestyle, and 'no event' padding by age); (b) UK Biobank (502,485 individuals, 80% train / 20% validation / longitudinal testing) and Danish registry (1,931,630 individuals) splits; (c) continuous age encoding, token embedding, N transformer blocks with causal continuous-time mask, weight tying, next-disease softmax head, and exponential time-to-event head; (d) example age:token prompt and sampled trajectory; (e-g) scaling laws, ablation, and predicted vs observed time to next token.

[paraphrase (visual p.4)] Figure 2 shows Delphi-2M multi-disease rate modelling and evaluation: (a) predicted vs observed age-stratified incidence rates for 9 diagnoses and death; (b-e) age-sex-stratified AUCs across n=906 male and n=957 female diagnoses by occurrence count, ICD-10 chapter, sex, and 0-120 month follow-up; (f) longitudinal test ROC curves for Death (Delphi AUC 0.81 vs Transformer 0.78, Charlson 0.73, Elixhauser 0.71, LLama3.1 0.69), Dementia (Delphi 0.82 vs UKBDRS 0.81), and CVD (Delphi 0.70 vs Qrisk3 0.71, Framingham/Score2/aPrevent 0.69); (g) comparison with MILTON biomarker model across n=410 diagnoses.

locator.section_or_table: A transformer model for health records

evidence_fragments.content: The first change therefore replaces GPT’s positional encoding, a mapping that identifies each text token’s discrete position, with an encoding of continuous age using sine and cosine basis functions16. Standard GPT models only predict the next token using a multinomial probability model. Thus, the second extension is the addition of another output head to also predict the time to the next token using an exponential waiting time model (Methods).

average age-stratified area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), which averages at values of approximately 0.76 in the internal validation data (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Table 2). For 97% of diagnoses, the AUC was greater than 0.5, indicating that the vast majority followed patterns with at least partial predictability. These patterns were found to be true across the different chapters of the ICD-10 spec trum, which define broad groups of disease for both sexes (Fig. 2c,d). Among the most confidently predicted next events is death, with an age-stratified AUC of 0.97 in both sexes.

In the first year of sampling, there are on average 17% disease tokens that are correctly predicted, and this drops to less than 14% 20 years later. These figures compare to values of 12–13% of correctly predicted disease tokens using sex and age alone, confirming that the conditional generation helps to make more accurate predictions of future events

capability_assessments.rationale: Continuous-time autoregressive generative transformer forecasting >1,000 disease rates and sampling 20-year health trajectories without action conditioning (L1).

limitations: Observational/unconditioned natural history forecasting; does not model causal treatment interventions.
Biases learned from UK Biobank/registry coding practices; no prospective clinical trial.
